key_insight: Generating possible protein–ligand binding poses is not enough—choosing the right one remains difficult. Pyrite introduces 1,500 pose pairs for evaluating ranking methods, with expert chemists performing near chance despite access to 3D visualization and physics-based scores.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to benchmark the ability to distinguish better protein–ligand binding poses among candidates generated by modern cofolding models.
method: Construct Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark containing 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein–ligand complexes.
Evaluate expert chemists using 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores.
Use pairwise ranking tasks to assess how reliably available chemical information supports pose selection.
impact: Pyrite provides a benchmark for testing AI pose-ranking agents in drug discovery. The near-chance expert performance underscores the difficulty of interpreting candidate poses and the need for more reliable ranking methods.
visual_elements: Side-by-side 3D views of two candidate ligand poses inside the same protein binding pocket.
Pipeline diagram: cofolding model → candidate poses → pairwise comparison → pose selection.
Benchmark overview graphic highlighting 1,500 pose pairs across diverse complexes.
Qualitative comparison of expert ranking performance against a chance baseline, without inventing numerical results.
paper_title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
paper_authors: Megha Srivastava, Michael H. Lim, Allison M. Keys, Pranav Murugan, Nate Gruver
